A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and are fully readable. Sections 1–9, Figures 1–5, Tables 1–10, and Appendices A.1–A.7 can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original multi-agent experiments with eight LLMs, selective automation and intervention results, private-thought analysis, and episode-length and agent-count ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results and analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The environment, Perfect-Play policy, Auto-Request/Auto-Fulfill decomposition, and three interventions are unchanged in Sections 2, 4, and 6. The agent prompts also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic information-sharing task and retain the same reasoning corpus and test scenarios. No dataset, domain, population, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same eight LLMs and Perfect-Play reference appear in corresponding comparisons. Comparator membership is unchanged across the baseline, decomposition, intervention, and ablation tables.

E3.justification: Both retain the default 10 agents, 20 rounds, 100 information pieces, two active tasks, and four required pieces per task. Metrics, intervention settings, and the 10/20/30-round and 10/20-agent ablation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The selective-automation analysis, private-thought classification, intervention analyses, and episode-length and agent-count ablations are retained with the same questions and evidence. Appendix A.7 also retains the same context example.

E5.justification: Both report five independent runs and 95% confidence intervals. Appendix A.2 retains the same 1,000-iteration bootstrap with seed 42, and the capability-correlation statistics and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain identical result entries and values, including o3's 34.4 ± 2.6 tasks and o3-mini's 102.8 ± 17.3 in Table 1. Figures 3–5 and the appendix reasoning and ablation findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same individual and group payoff definitions, environment assumptions, and approximate perfect-play ceiling derivation. No mathematical definition, argument, or proof is substantively revised.

C1.justification: The rewritten abstract preserves the capability–cooperation disconnect, cooperation-versus-competence decomposition, and targeted-intervention claims. Its emphasis on active withholding already appears in v1's introduction and conclusion; contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism interpretations, the caveat about private thoughts rationalizing decisions, and visibility and scaling qualifications remain unchanged. The new Impact Statement repeats deployment implications already expressed in v1's discussion and conclusion.

D1.justification: Appendices A.5–A.7 retain the same API-temperature disclosure, configuration details, action formats, scaffolding prompt, and context example. Both versions state plans to release the codebase; no new implementation or access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 7 preserves the same cited works and research positioning. Updates to Cowell's year and edition, AgentBench's author list, and Bernstein's DOI are bibliographic metadata changes rather than changes in literature coverage.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract, adds a short Impact Statement, makes small wording corrections, and updates affiliation, publication, and bibliographic text. The main sections and appendix subsections retain their order and essentially all other prose.

P2.justification: The single-column workshop format becomes a two-column conference layout for the main text and references. Title and author formatting, headers, citation styling, and figure/table sizes and placements change throughout; the single-column appendices also reflow. All five figures and ten tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The revision primarily changes the publication layout and provides localized editorial polish. The rewritten abstract and new Impact Statement summarize existing claims, while all results, analyses, qualifications, and reproducibility details remain intact. Overall readability and scientific support remain essentially equivalent.
